name: Mantisfolk
body:
A species of powerful humanoid insects, mantisfolk are indigenous to warm grasslands, where they live as itinerant hunters. Despite a sizeable population, they are not well known, as they are reclusive and rarely leave their homeland or engage with other sentient species. Most humanoids find them quite alien in their outlook as well as in their appearance. While they make formidable foes, mantisfolk do not usually attack other sentient creatures without provocation.

Physical

A mantisfolk looks very similar to a bipedal praying mantis, standing as tall as a human.

The females are somewhat larger than the males on average. They have six limbs: two that serve as legs and four as arms.

Mantisfolk have both internal and external skeletal structures. Internally, they have a cartilaginous skeleton much like a shark, which supports them while giving them a great deal of flexibility. This is reinforced by a thin but rigid exoskeleton, which usually matches their homeland in coloration—brown, yellow, or sand color for mantisfolk native to the scrub and plains, or bright greens for those who live in the jungle.

Two compound eyes, two antennae, and a complicated jaw structure, which includes a pair of wicked mandibles, give the head an insect-like appearance. The typical mantisfolk wears a number of belts and slings for holding its equipment, but no other clothing or armor. The rare mantisfolk who adventures with humanoids may be the exception to this rule.

Social

Most humanoids consider mantisfolk to be alien, inscrutable beings. Their faces are not capable of showing much emotion—at least not any that humans and their ilk can detect—although someone familiar with the species may be able to detect their level of comfort or agitation by the motion of their antennae and mandibles.

Most mantisfolk live a simple existence.

Their lives are short, often brutal, and are focused almost exclusively on the task of survival. A colony will follow the strongest among them, but they have no loyalty to their leader; they merely recognize strength for what it is.

Mantisfolk do not take foolish risks, but will not hesitate to attack if they perceive a danger to themselves or their hunting grounds. While they rarely interact with humanoids, negotiation is a better tactic—if a difficult one—than attacking these creatures head-on.

Alignment and Religion

Mantisfolk are usually Chaotic Neutral. They are not concerned about issues of Good or Evil, only about survival. While they are good at cooperating, ultimately each mantisfolk considers itself a nation of one, participating in its pack only to further its own interests.

Mantisfolk have no established religious practices of their own, with most being apathetic toward such things. However, some of them have become attuned to the hunting and resource aspects of nature deities, and druidism holds a certain appeal to some of them.

Names

Some typical mantisfolk names include the following (choose or roll 1d12):

An-Ki-Ni-Ti
Chaka-Kaa
Chan-Tik
Chapa-Kita
Ha-Ta-Ki-Ti
Ka-Kiri
Ka-Pa-Che
Krik-Kit
Pa-Ki-Ri-Ki
Tichi-Pika
Tik-Taak
Wa-Tu-Chi
Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are agile and perceptive, but off-putting. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Dex, +2 Wis, –2 Cha [standard]. (0)
Size Medium. As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size. (0)
Type You are a Monstrous humanoid. (3)
Speed Your base speed is 30 feet. (0)
Languages You begin play speaking Common and Aklo. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Draconic, Dromite, Elven, Gnoll, Goblin, and Halfling. (0)
Other Traits
Camouflage Your exoskeleton’s coloration and texture provide you with natural camouflage. Pick one type of terrain available to rangers as a favored terrain. You gain a +4 species bonus to Stealth checks while in your selected terrain type. (1)
Claws You can use your primary arms to make two claw attacks. These are primary natural attacks that deal 1d4 damage each. Note that your secondary arms cannot be used to make claw attacks. (2)
Senses Darkvision. You have darkvision 60 feet. (—)
Jumper You are always considered to have a running start when making an Acrobatics check to jump. (2)
Natural Armor Your exoskeleton is tough and resistant to blows, providing you with a +1 natural armor bonus. (2)
Secondary Arms You have a second pair of arms set below your primary arms. These secondary arms can be used to carry objects, but they are not strong enough to wield shields or weapons. You can use your secondary arms for the somatic components of casting spells. You can also use them to retrieve small, stowed objects carried on your person as a swift action. (2)
Weapon Familiarity You are proficient with the starknife and the trident, and you treat the double trident* as a martial weapon instead of an exotic one. (1)
Total: 13 RP (Advanced)
Variants
Mantisfolk Brute

You were exposed to special chemicals as a larvae that mutated you into a hulking brute of an adult. You are very strong physically—but greatly compromised mentally. You gain +4 Str, –2 Int, –2 Wis, –4 Cha. This alters ability score modifiers.

Mantisfolk Intellectual

You are not as physically strong as most of your kin, but you make up for any physical shortcomings with your commanding intellect. You gain +2 Int, +2 Wis, –2 Str. This alters ability score modifiers.

Alternate Species Traits
Feral You never bothered to train with manufactured weapons, instead learning to use your mandibles to make a savage bite attack. This is a primary natural attack that deals 1d4 damage. This trait replaces weapon familiarity.
Gliding Wings You have a pair of wings that allow you to fall from any distance without taking damage (as if subject to a constant nonmagical feather fall spell). While in midair, you can move up to 5 feet in any horizontal direction for every 1 foot you fall, at a speed of 60 feet per round. You cannot gain height with these wings alone; you merely coast in other directions as you fall. If subjected to a strong wind or any other effect that causes you to rise, you can take advantage of the updraft to increase the distance you can glide. This trait replaces camouflage and natural armor.
Limited Telepathy You can communicate telepathically with any creatures within 30 feet with whom you share a language in common. Otherwise, this ability is identical to the telepathy ability. This trait replaces jumper and weapon familiarity.
Psionics You gain Wild Talent as a bonus feat at 1st level. If you take levels in a psionic class, you instead gain the Psionic Talent feat. In addition, You can use the following psi-like powers once per day each: chameleon, know direction and location, and your choice of either metaphysical claw or prevenom. The manifester level for these powers is equal to 1/2 your character level (minimum 1), and Wisdom is your manifesting ability. This trait replaces jumper and natural armor.
Sleep Immunity You do not sleep. You must still rest quietly for 8 hours while refraining from strenuous activity in order to recover hit points, spell slots, and so on. You are immune to magic sleep effects. This trait replaces camouflage.
Toxic A number of times per day equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1/day), you can envenom one of your natural attacks (such as your mandibles or a claw) or a weapon that you wield with venom from a sac near your mouth. Applying venom in this way is a swift action. This trait replaces camouflage.

Mantisfolk Venom: Injury; save Fort DC 10 + 1/2 your Hit Dice + your Constitution modifier; frequency 1/round for 6 rounds; effect 1d2 Dex; cure 1 save.

Feats
Chameleon Camouflage

You can change the color of your exoskeleton to blend into your surroundings.

Prerequisites: Mantisfolk, camouflage species trait.

Benefit: If you spend a full-round action, you can adjust the color and texture of your carapace to match whatever terrain you find yourself in. You gain a +4 species bonus to Stealth checks in that type of terrain until you use this ability to change your coloration again.

Strong Arms

Your secondary arms are strong enough to use for attacking.

Prerequisites: Mantisfolk, secondary arms species trait.

Benefit: You can use your secondary arms to make claw attacks, although they are still not as powerful as your primary arms. These are always secondary attacks that deal 1d3 damage plus 1/2 your Strength bonus.

Favored Class Bonuses
Barbarian Add a +1/2 bonus to your trap sense and a +1/2 bonus to Acrobatics checks to jump while raging.
Brawler Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a reposition or trip attempt.
Cleric Select one domain power granted at 1st level that is normally usable a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Wisdom modifier. Add +1/2 to the number of uses per day of that domain power.
Druid Add +1/2 to your vermin empathy bonus. You must have the vermin empathy ability to select this benefit.
Fighter Add +1 foot to the range increment of any one thrown weapon with which you are already proficient. This has no effect unless you select this benefit five times (or another increment of five).
Gunslinger Add a +1/2 bonus on Acrobatics checks when you have at least 1 grit point.
Hunter Add 1 hit point to your animal companion. If you replace your animal companion, the new companion gains these bonus hit points.
Kineticist Gain a +1/4 bonus on damage rolls that apply your elemental overflow bonus.
Marksman Add +1/3 to damage rolls made with thrown weapons when expending your psionic focus on Psionic Shot.
Psion Add a +1/2 bonus on concentration checks when manifesting powers from your discipline list.
Psychic Warrior Add +1 to your power points per day.
Ranger Choose a weapon from the following list: bite, claws, double trident*, trident, or starknife. Add +1/2 on critical hit confirmation rolls made while using that weapon (maximum bonus of +4). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Rogue Gain a +1/2 bonus on Bluff checks to feint and on Acrobatics checks to jump.
Slayer Gains +1/6 of a new slayer talent.
Soulknife Add +1/3 on critical hit confirmation rolls made with your mindblade (maximum bonus of +5). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Wizard Select one arcane school power at 1st level that is normally usable a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Intelligence modifier. Add +1/2 to the number of uses per day of that arcane school power.
Mantisfolk Equipment
Double Trident (exotic weapon)

This rare exotic weapon has a two- or three-pronged trident at each end and is specially weighted to allow it to be thrown. Primitive mantisfolk often make the heads from fragile materials such as obsidian or bone, but a skilled weaponsmith can also manufacture them from metal.

Double trident 50 gp 1d6/1d6 1d8/1d8 ×2 10 ft. 10 lbs. P / P Double, Spear, Thrown, Two-Handed
